newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures pulled higher by Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures pulled higher by Treasuries.

text.p: German bonds and bund futures posted careful gains in morning trading, the market buoyed by solid gains in U.S. Treasuries, but held back by mark weakness.
Dealers said the weak mark meant the German market was unable to match the Treasury market's rally -- and could also fall further in the event of a downward correction in the U.S.

This meant prices were likely to hold at around the higher levels seen in early trade until the U.S. market opened, but not go much further, they said. "We almost fell out of the upward trend yesterday. But, critically, the bund future went above 102.53 this morning and held there," one trader said.

The September bund contract was trading 0.36 point higher at 102.80 at 0915 GMT, bumping up against resistance at that level. The July 2007 10-year benchmark bund was trading at 103.22 for a yield of 5.56 percent.

Dealers said the market was now waiting for data from the U.S. due this afternoon. Building starts for June and weekly jobs data is due at 1230 GMT, while the Philadelphia Fed index is due at 1400 GMT.
